Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
# Summary of the 2024 Manifesto

This manifesto outlines a comprehensive policy platform focused on five key themes: economy, public services, environment, international relations, and democratic reform.

## Economy and Business

The economic platform prioritises responsible fiscal management, green infrastructure investment, and improved trading relationships with European neighbours. Key proposals include replacing business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy, expanding apprenticeships, creating Lifelong Skills Grants of £5,000 per adult, and supporting small businesses through improved access to capital. Employment reforms include establishing a "dependent contractor" status for gig economy workers, improving sick pay provisions, and expanding parental leave.

## Healthcare and Social Care

Healthcare proposals centre on guaranteeing GP appointments within seven days, recruiting 8,000 additional GPs, and ensuring cancer treatment begins within 62 days of urgent referral. Mental health provisions include establishing youth mental health hubs in every community and placing qualified professionals in all schools. Social care reforms include introducing free personal care, creating a Royal College of Care Workers, and establishing a higher minimum wage for care workers. The manifesto proposes a cross-party commission on sustainable social care funding.

## Education

Education commitments include increasing per-pupil funding above inflation, providing mental health professionals in every school, reinstating maintenance grants for disadvantaged students, and introducing a tutoring guarantee for disadvantaged pupils. Early years proposals include additional free hours for disadvantaged children and tripling the Early Years Pupil Premium.

## Environment and Energy

Environmental priorities include achieving net zero emissions by 2045, investing in home insulation programmes, targeting 90% renewable electricity generation by 2030, and ending sewage pollution through transforming water companies into public benefit companies. The manifesto proposes doubling protected areas, woodland cover, and species abundance by 2050.

## Housing

Housing proposals target building 380,000 homes annually, including 150,000 social homes, through new garden cities and community development. Renter protections include banning no-fault evictions and creating a national landlord register. The manifesto proposes abolishing residential leasehold and introducing a Rent-to-Own scheme.

## Criminal Justice

Policing reforms include restoring community policing, guaranteeing police attendance at all burglaries, and creating an Online Crime Agency. The manifesto proposes reducing court backlogs, improving prison rehabilitation, and adopting a public health approach to youth violence.

## Immigration

Immigration reforms include transferring work visa policy from the Home Office, clearing asylum backlogs within three months, allowing asylum seekers to work after three months, and establishing safe legal routes for refugees. The manifesto proposes scrapping the Rwanda scheme and ending immigration detention for children.

## Democratic Reform

Constitutional proposals include introducing proportional representation for elections, votes for 16-17 year olds, and reforming the House of Lords. The manifesto advocates for a federal structure with devolved powers, enshrining the Ministerial Code in law, and capping political donations.

## International Affairs

Foreign policy priorities include supporting Ukraine, restoring international development spending to 0.7% of national income, and rebuilding European relationships through a four-stage roadmap. Defence commitments include reversing army cuts and increasing spending toward 2.5% of GDP while maintaining NATO membership and nuclear deterrent.
